Forecast Discussion

Low pressure moves north just off the Carolina and Virginia coasts today. Damp air on its west side keeps light rain and drizzle going, with areas of fog. The fog lingers tonight.

A weak cold front crosses from the west Monday morning. Fog early gives way to a mostly cloudy day. Northwest winds behind the front may bring a few showers, mostly along the western escarpment near the NC/TN border.

Colder, drier air arrives Monday night. Tuesday is dry as high pressure builds in from the northwest.

That high shifts to New England by Wednesday and wedges cold air down the east side of the Appalachians. Wednesday is cold and gray. Low pressure develops along the Gulf coast, and rain develops late in the day. The highest elevations may see a brief mix with snow as it begins, but we expect no accumulation.

The low moves up the Carolina coast Wednesday night and Thanksgiving Day. Rain continues Wednesday night and Thanksgiving morning, then tapers off in the afternoon.

Colder air follows on northwest winds Thursday night. Snow showers are possible, mostly at higher elevations near the NC/TN border, and a flurry may linger into early Friday.

The rest of Friday is dry and colder. Saturday stays dry and cool as high pressure takes control of the Eastern U.S.
